 CNY weather: Rainy weekend, possible snow next week
 Published: Nov. 07, 2026, 7:10 a.m. 
 Temperatures will drop in stages across the Northeast through mid-November, with cool, showery weather this weekend that could give way to more widespread rain and snow showers later next week. Accuweather 
 Set as Google Preferred Source 
 By Syracuse.com Express Desk 
 Scattered rain showers will continue across Central New York on Saturday, with temperatures beginning a cooling trend into the 40s and 50s through Monday.
 The National Weather Service says showers will become more isolated by midday Saturday for most areas, though Syracuse and the Tug Hill region may see continued showers through the day. Lake moisture could bring additional scattered showers into Sunday as northwesterly winds develop.
 Gusty winds are expected most days, with the potential for gusts of 20 mph or higher at times through early next week. Temperatures will generally remain in the 40s and 50s through Monday as the northwest flow pattern continues.
 A shortwave passing through the area Monday should renew the potential for showers, likely aided by moisture from Lake Ontario. A brief break in shower activity is possible Tuesday and Wednesday, though clearing may be slower than initially forecast.

 Looking ahead to late next week, meteorologists are tracking a potentially impactful weather system. A clipper-type system is forecast to dive into the plains and Ohio Valley by Thursday.
 The National Weather Service notes there is considerable uncertainty with this system, but rain chances have increased for Thursday through Friday. Temperatures could support a wintry mix as well, with higher elevations favored for rain and slushy snow if the storm ends up south of the region.
 The weather pattern over the next week will bring several disturbances in a broad northwest flow, keeping conditions unsettled with mainly rain showers into early next week. Forecasters say this could potentially be followed by the season’s first snowflakes late next week, though significant uncertainty remains about that longer-range forecast.
